title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
slides: Who pays when OpenCode gets hacked?
Attackers abused exposed credentials to run paid AI queries
Users faced unexpected charges on accounts they trusted
Check your OpenCode keys and billing history today
Rotate credentials before the next silent charge hits
thread_text:
1. Who foots the bill for exposed keys?

Attackers used leaked OpenCode credentials to run paid AI queries on other people's accounts. The victims only found out when charges appeared.

2. Silent charges from someone else's usage

Exposed API keys let attackers rack up AI queries without triggering alerts. Users saw unexpected charges on accounts they trusted.

3. Trusted accounts, unexpected bills

OpenCode billed users for queries they never ran. The breach wasn't in the model, it was in the keys left exposed.

4. Check your keys and billing now

Look for unfamiliar activity in OpenCode billing history. If you see queries you didn't make, your credentials may already be compromised.

5. Rotate credentials before the next charge

Change your OpenCode keys today. Don't wait for another silent charge to confirm what's already exposed.
